documents.t: The caption identifying each small multiple. The card applies to the Small multiples layout only — concentric rings share one chart area and are identified by the legend instead. Property Description Default Show Series Titles Master toggle On Position Top or Bottom of each chart Top Font Family, size, bold, italic, underline Segoe UI 11, bold Text Color Fixed color of the caption #333333 Assign series color to font color Paints the caption with the series color instead Off Title Display Text, Logo and Text, or Logo Text Logo Width / Height Size of the logo, in pixels 20 × 20 Series logos (JSON) Lookup mapping each series name to a base64 image (empty)

The list maps an exact series name to a base64 image: [ { "label": "France", "logo": "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KG..." }, { "label": "Germany", "logo": "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KG..." } ] Two ways to fill it: The picture icon on the visual (edit mode, small multiples with several series) opens an editor pre-filled with one row per series — paste a base64 image next to each name. The fx button binds a DAX measure that builds the whole list, which is the better option when the images already live in a lookup table: Series Logos JSON = "[" & CONCATENATEX ( VALUES ( Markets[market_name] ), "{""label"":""" & Markets[market_name] & """,""logo"":""" & MAX ( Markets[flag_base64] ) & """}", "," ) & "]" A label that matches no series is ignored, a duplicate label keeps its first entry, and malformed JSON simply yields no logo — the lookup never breaks a render. Entries go through the same base64 validation as every other image field: external URLs are rejected. The lookup wins over the Logo role for the titles, so a per-category logo can paint the slices and the legend while the lookup paints the titles.

Logo and Text and Logo need the Logo field well to return a base64-encoded image for the legend value — a flag for a chart per country, a brand mark for a chart per brand. Use the Series logos lookup A title logo identifies the legend value, which the Logo role cannot name: a column dropped there joins the category axis, and a measure costs one evaluation per cell. Use the Series logos (JSON) field below instead — resolved once per render, and it keeps the two sets of images apart. When no image is available for a series, that title falls back to plain text rather than leaving a hole in the grid. Titles longer than the chart cell are truncated with an ellipsis, measured against the real font, so a long series name never overlaps its neighbour.

Every series is compared to one reference series, category by category. The question the card answers is "is this slice a significantly bigger share here than in the reference?". The card runs up to three independent tests. A General group holds the settings they share and switches each test on; each test then has its own group. General Property Description Default Activate significance tests Master toggle Off Significance Level 90 %, 95 % or 99 % 95 % Test On Shares or Means Shares Variance Method Pooled or Separate (shares only) Pooled Test 1 / Test 2 / Test 3 None, vs. Reference series or External reference Test 1: vs. Reference series — Tests 2 and 3: None Icon Size (px) Size of the icons and texts 12 Test 1, Test 2, Test 3 Property Description Default Reference series (regex) vs. Reference series — picks the reference by its legend name (empty) Reference measure (regex) / Apply to measure (regex) External reference — see External reference (empty) Match status Read-only: what was resolved, or why nothing was — Display mode Icon, Slice outline, Label background or Text Icon Positive / Negative color Colors of the two directions Green / red Custom icon positive / negative Base64 images replacing the default arrows — Icon mode (empty) Positive / Negative text Texts written for the two directions — Text mode + / - Test 1 keeps the settings of the former one-test card, so a report built before the three tests keeps its test unchanged.

On a pie the quantity that compares across charts is the share, not the raw value: two pies built on different bases are only comparable once each slice is expressed as a fraction of its own total. The Shares test therefore runs a two-proportion test on value / series total, which is already a proportion — no rescaling of percentages is applied here. The Means test keeps the raw values and uses the Standard Deviation field, since a mean is not a share. Slices of the same pie are never tested against each other: parts of one total are not independent, and a two-sample test between them would be wrong.

The Base field must be filled with the sample size behind each slice. Without it the vs. Reference series tests are disabled and Match status says so (an external reference carrying its own ttest or signif needs no base). A slice whose base is missing or zero on either side of the comparison is left untested.

The reference is chosen by a case-insensitive regular expression on the legend name — for example Total or ^Market$. The first matching series wins, and it is itself excluded from the decoration. Match status reports the resolved series, an empty match, or an invalid expression.

A test set to External reference compares each slice with a measure of the Significance reference role, evaluated by Power BI for that same slice — last year, a benchmark, another scope — without that data having to be in the chart. The measure returns a small JSON that tells the visual either what to test ({"val", "n"}, {"val", "n", "stddev"}) or the result to display ({"ttest"}, {"signif"}). See External reference. On a pie the test runs on shares: with {"val", "n"}, val must be a share (0..1) as well.

Mode Result Icon A ▲ or ▼ just outside the slice, replaceable by your own base64 images Slice outline The slice border takes the color of the direction Label background The data label of the slice gets a colored background Text A short text (+ / - by default, or any letter or emoji) in the color of the direction, just outside the slice When several tests decorate the same slice with icons or texts, they queue up outwards. With several Slice outline tests on one slice, the first one draws the border. Slice outline is overridden on any slice that the Highlight card is outlining — the highlight is the louder signal and wins the border.

A radial mark drawn at the angle carrying a target value — the visual equivalent of a goal line on a bar chart, and what turns a half donut into a gauge. Property Description Default Show target line Master toggle Off Target value The value to mark (empty) Target unit Value or Percentage of total Value Extent Ring only or Full radius Ring only Color Line color #C62828 Width (px) Line thickness 3 Style Solid, dashed or dotted Solid Overhang (px) How far the line sticks out past each end 3

Setting The angle is computed as Value target / total of the series — the target is expressed in the units of the measure Percentage of total target / 100 — the target is a share, from 0 to 100 Targets outside the range are clamped to the ends of the chart rather than wrapping around.

Target value carries the fx button. A rule bound to the legend field gives each series its own target, which is what makes a grid of small multiples or a stack of concentric rings comparable against their individual goals. The value typed in the card is used for any series the rule leaves empty.

Setting The line runs Ring only From the inner to the outer edge of each ring, so every ring shows its own target Full radius From the centre to the outer edge, one line across the whole chart Ring only is meaningful on a donut; on a full pie the ring already reaches the centre and the setting is hidden.

The SDM Smart Pie Chart renders a composition as a pie, a donut, or a half-circle gauge — or, in its concentric type, as radial bars. Each category is a value of the Category field; each value of the Legend field adds a whole chart to a grid of small multiples.

Three shapes — full circle, top half circle and bottom half circle. A half circle is not a cropped pie: the whole series is laid out over 180°, so every slice keeps its share of the total Pie or donut — an adjustable inner radius turns the pie into a donut, which unlocks the center label Small multiples — one chart per legend value, with a cap on the number of charts per row; a partial last row stays centred Concentric rings — a second chart type: one ring per category, each starting at zero and scaled to the largest value, for magnitudes that do not add up to a whole Regex highlighting — pull one or more slices out of the crowd by exploding them, outlining them, or dimming the others Target line — a radial mark at the angle carrying a target value, as a value or as a percentage of the total Center label — the total, or any caption, in the hole of a donut Data-driven colors and logos — the Series Color field colors either the slices or the charts; the Logo field feeds the legend, the slices themselves (inside or outside) and the series titles Significance testing — up to three tests, each comparing every series to a reference series category by category on its shares, or to an external reference Cross-filtering — click or Ctrl+click a slice to filter other visuals Tooltips — category, value, share, base and custom tooltip measures on hover Series Threshold — a publication rule applied one small multiple at a time: a market whose smallest base falls short is flagged, or withdrawn and replaced by a message, while its neighbours keep being drawn Note — a caption box over the chart, with %MIN(field) style formulas and an alert that fires under a threshold Global Threshold — clears the chart on an empty dataset, or when a base is too small to be published

Data Role Description Category One slice per value Values The measure sliced by the pie Legend Splits the data into one chart per value, laid out as a grid of small multiples Series Color A measure or column returning a hex color, read per category or per legend value Logo A measure or column returning a base64 image, read per category (legend and slice logos) and per legend value (series titles) Base Sample size, required by the significance tests Standard Deviation Used by the significance test on means Significance reference Reference of an External reference significance test, as JSON — not drawn Tooltips Extra measures added to the tooltip

A pie divides a whole, so a negative contribution has no angle to occupy: negative values are plotted as zero. They stay available to the significance test on means, which works on the raw value rather than on the share. Blank values are simply absent from the chart.

The Data Colors card overrides the colors resolved from the data. Which entries appear depends on Apply colors to in the Radar card: Threads — one color picker per legend value Axes — one color picker per axis Property Description Default Default Color Fallback color #4682B4 One picker per series or per axis Overrides the color resolved from the data Resolved color Each picker carries the fx button, so a color can be driven by a conditional formatting rule rather than a fixed value.

Colors are resolved in this order, the first match winning: Conditional formatting (fx) set on the picker below The Series Color field, read on the dimension selected by Apply colors to The Power BI host palette The built-in ten-color SDM palette One dimension at a time The Series Color field and these pickers always target the same dimension. Switching Apply colors to swaps the whole list — the pickers of the other dimension are not lost, they are simply not shown while that dimension is not the one being colored.

The field expects a hex code such as #FF0000, returned by a measure or a column. Feeding colors from the model is the practical way to keep a series the same color across every report page, and to drive colors from a lookup table rather than from the visual. Because the field is read on one dimension only, switching Apply colors to re-reads the same field on the other dimension — there is no second field to fill in. The side that is not data-driven falls back to its single fixed color: Axis Color in the Axes card, or Thread Color in the Radar card.

The Legend card lists the series (the threads of the web). It is hidden automatically when there is only one series. Property Description Default Show Legend Show or hide the legend On Position Top, Bottom, or Left / Right aligned to the top, centre or bottom Top Font Family, size, bold, italic, underline Segoe UI 11 Assign series color to font color Print each label in its series color Off

Top and Bottom lay the legend out horizontally across the full width, centred. The four side positions stack the entries vertically in a column capped at 150 px wide, aligned to the top, the middle or the bottom of the plot area. The web takes whatever space is left, and shrinks to keep its axis labels inside the viewport.

Logos come from the Logo field, read per legend value. The same field also feeds the axis-end logos, read per axis. Property Description Default Legend Display Text, Logo and Text, or Logo Text Text Wrap Ellipsis (one line, ends with …) or Wrap (flows onto several lines). Never scrolls. Ellipsis Logo Width / Logo Height Size of the logo in pixels 20 × 20 The color swatch is always drawn, so the legend stays readable in Logo mode. Entries without an image fall back to text, so a partially filled Logo field still produces a readable legend. Colors applied to the axes When the Radar card applies colors to the axes, every thread shares one color — the legend swatches are then all identical, which is expected: the series are told apart by their label or logo, not by their color.

A legend box is bounded: 150 px wide when it sits on the left or the right, the width of the visual when it sits on top or below. Text Wrap decides what happens to an entry that does not fit. Mode Result Ellipsis (default) The entry stays on one line and ends with an ellipsis Wrap The entry flows onto as many lines as it needs Neither mode ever produces a scrollbar. A scrollbar inside a report tile hides entries behind a control nobody thinks to drag, so it was removed outright. Entries that no longer fit With scrolling gone, a legend taller than the space it has is clipped rather than scrolled. Wrap makes entries taller and so clips sooner than Ellipsis — give the legend a horizontal position, or shorten the labels, when every series has to stay visible.
The Radar card controls the geometry of the web, how the threads are drawn, and which dimension the data-driven colors are applied to.
Property Description Default Start Angle Rotates the whole web, in degrees. 0 puts the first axis at 12 o'clock. 0 Direction Clockwise or Counter-clockwise ordering of the axes Clockwise

The Series Color field feeds one dimension at a time — either the threads or the axes, never both. This dropdown decides which. Property Description Default Thread Width Stroke width in pixels. 0 hides the outline — useful with Fill Area on. 2 Thread Style Solid, Dashed or Dotted Solid Line Shape Straight joins the vertices with segments; Smooth rounds the polygon into a closed cardinal curve Straight Show Markers Draw a dot at each vertex On Marker Size Marker radius in pixels 4 Missing values A series with no value on one axis simply skips that vertex — the thread short-cuts across the missing spoke instead of collapsing to the centre.

Below about 40 % the topmost series hides the ones behind it.
The Scale card decides how values are mapped onto the radius of each axis. This is what lets a score out of 50 and a score out of 10 sit on the same web without one crushing the other.

Property Description Default Scale Mode Per axis gives every axis its own range, taken from the values observed on that axis alone. Shared gives every axis the same range, the union of all observed values. Per axis Graduations depend on this The Web and Circles graduation styles join equal radii across axes, which only means something when every axis shares one scale. With Per axis they fall back to Ticks — see Graduations.

Property Description Default Start at Zero Pull the minimum of each axis down to zero (or to the data minimum if it is negative) Off Range Padding Widen the range by this percentage so vertices do not sit exactly on the outer ring. When Start at Zero is on, only the top is pushed out — zero stays pinned. 5 % Inner Radius Hollow out the centre of the web, as a percentage of the outer radius. The axis minimum then sits on that inner ring. 0 % Values falling outside the resolved range are clamped, so a thread never escapes the web.

In edit mode, a gear icon appears in the top-right corner of the visual. It opens a dialog with one row per axis and a Minimum / Maximum field on each. The fields are pre-filled with the bounds currently in use, so confirming the dialog pins every axis at once. Bounds are stored as JSON on the visual and survive refreshes; clearing a value returns that axis to automatic scaling. When to pin bounds Pin the bounds when the axes are rating scales with a known ceiling — a score out of 10 should be plotted against 0..10, not against the range the current filter happens to produce.

Every series is compared to one reference series, axis by axis. The question the card answers is "does this profile sit significantly above or below the reference on this criterion?". The card runs up to three independent tests. A General group holds the settings they share and switches each test on; each test then has its own group. General Property Description Default Activate significance tests Master toggle Off Significance Level 90 %, 95 % or 99 % 95 % Test On Percentages or Means Percentages Variance Method Pooled or Separate (percentages only) Pooled Test 1 / Test 2 / Test 3 None, vs. Reference series or External reference Test 1: vs. Reference series — Tests 2 and 3: None Icon Size (px) Size of the icons and texts 12 Test 1, Test 2, Test 3 Property Description Default Reference series (regex) vs. Reference series — picks the reference by its legend name (empty) Reference measure (regex) / Apply to measure (regex) External reference — see External reference (empty) Match status Read-only: what was resolved, or why nothing was — Display mode Icon, Marker, Label background or Text Icon Positive / Negative color Colors of the two directions Green / red Custom icon positive / negative Base64 images replacing the default arrows — Icon mode (empty) Positive / Negative text Texts written for the two directions — Text mode + / - Test 1 keeps the settings of the former one-test card, so a report built before the three tests keeps its test unchanged.

Only series against series, on the same axis. Two axes of a radar carry their own unit and their own scale, so a comparison across spokes would be meaningless — the card does not offer one. The Percentages test is a two-proportion test. Proportions must be expressed on 0..1, while Power BI measures usually carry them on 0..100: when either of the two compared values exceeds 1, the pair is divided by 100 before the test. No manual conversion is needed, and a measure already on 0..1 is left alone. The Means test keeps the raw values and uses the Standard Deviation field. It has no variance method to choose, so that dropdown disappears.

The Base field must be filled with the sample size behind each value. Without it the vs. Reference series tests are disabled and Match status says so (an external reference carrying its own ttest or signif needs no base). A vertex whose base is missing or zero on either side of the comparison is left untested, as is one where either series has no value on that axis.

The reference is chosen by a case-insensitive regular expression on the legend name — for example Total or ^Market$. The first matching series wins, and it is itself excluded from the decoration: the reference is never marked against itself. Match status reports the resolved series, an empty match, or an invalid expression, so a typo in the pattern never fails silently.

A test set to External reference compares each vertex with a measure of the Significance reference role, evaluated by Power BI for that same vertex — last year, a benchmark, another scope — without that data having to be in the chart. The measure returns a small JSON that tells the visual either what to test ({"val", "n"}, {"val", "n", "stddev"}) or the result to display ({"ttest"}, {"signif"}). See External reference.

Mode Result Icon A ▲ or ▼ just beyond the vertex, clear of both the marker and the data label, replaceable by your own base64 images Marker A dot in the color of the direction is drawn over the vertex, covering the series marker. With Show Markers off it becomes a dot on the significant vertices only Label background The data label of the vertex gets a colored background Text A short text (+ / - by default, or any letter or emoji) in the color of the direction, where the icon would be When several tests decorate the same vertex with icons or texts, they queue up outwards, beyond the vertex. Label background needs the Data Labels card to be on — it colors the label rather than drawing anything of its own, and it replaces the background configured there on the vertices that came out significant.

The Tooltip card controls the hover tooltip of the radar. Property Description Default Show Tooltips Show or hide the tooltip On The radar uses the native Power BI tooltip, so it inherits the report theme and honours report page tooltips configured at the report level.

The tooltip is triggered by an invisible circle centred on each vertex, slightly wider than the marker itself. It works whether or not Show Markers is on in the Radar card — hiding the markers hides the dots, not the tooltip. Markers and cross-filtering Cross-filtering, on the other hand, does depend on the markers: clicking a vertex to filter the rest of the report requires Show Markers to be on, since the marker is the click target.

Each tooltip lists, in order: The axis name, as the header The series name and its value on that axis, in the series color The Base, when the Base field well is filled Any measure dropped in the Tooltips field well Values are formatted with the Display Units and Decimals chosen in the Data Labels card, so the tooltip and the printed labels always agree — even when the labels themselves are hidden.

The SDM Smart Radar draws a spider web over n axes. Each axis carries its own scale, so a score out of 50 and a score out of 10 can sit side by side on the same web without one crushing the other — the observed minimum and maximum of each axis define its range.

Independent per-axis scales — every axis is scaled from its own min/max, with an optional shared mode when all axes really do share a unit Manual axis bounds — a modal editor (gear icon, edit mode) pins the minimum and maximum of any axis Data-driven colors — the Series Color field colors either the threads or the axes; the Data Colors card overrides whichever side the field is applied to Logos — the Logo field feeds both the legend and the outer end of each axis Area fill — optional filled polygons with an adjustable transparency Graduations — ticks on the spokes, a web joining equal graduations, or concentric circles Significance testing — up to three tests, each comparing every series to a reference series axis by axis, or to an external reference (last year, a benchmark…) Cross-filtering — click or Ctrl+click a vertex marker to filter other visuals Tooltips — axis, series value, base and custom tooltip measures on hover

Data Role Description Axis One spoke of the web per value. Each axis carries its own scale. Values The measure plotted along each axis Legend Splits the web into one thread per series Series Color A measure or column returning a hex color, read per legend value or per axis Logo A measure or column returning a base64 image, read per legend value and per axis Base Sample size, required by the significance tests Standard Deviation Standard deviation, used by the significance test on means Significance reference Reference of an External reference significance test, as JSON — not drawn Tooltips Extra measures added to the hover tooltip

Three spokes are the point at which a web starts to enclose an area and read as a profile. Fewer are still drawn — two axes give a flat web, one gives a single spoke with its marker — because refusing to plot data the visual can place would leave an unexplained blank. The chart is simply not saying much yet.

A series with no value on one axis simply skips that vertex: the thread short-cuts across the missing spoke instead of dropping to the centre, which would read as a zero. Values falling outside the range resolved for their axis are clamped to the inner or outer ring, so a thread never escapes the web. This only happens with manual bounds — the automatic range always covers the data.

Cards are listed in the order they appear in the formatting pane. Card What it controls Radar Geometry, thread rendering, area fill, the color-target switch Axes Spokes, category labels and axis-end logos Scale Per-axis vs shared scaling, padding, manual bounds Graduations Ticks, web or circles, and graduation values Data Colors Per-series or per-axis color pickers Legend Position, font and logo display Data Labels Vertex value labels Tooltip What appears on hover Significance Reference-series comparison The Empty data and License cards are shared by every visual of the suite — see Licensing.

The scatter plot supports analytics lines on both axes. Unlike standard Power BI visuals, which allow adding multiple instances of each line type, custom visuals are limited by the API to one instance per line type. To compensate, the SDM Scatter Plot offers a Both axis option that draws the same statistic on both X and Y axes simultaneously. X Constant Line / Y Constant Line — User-defined constant values Min Line, Max Line, Median Line, Average Line — Each with an axis choice: X Axis, Y Axis, or Both Symmetry Shading — Highlights the area where Y > X or Y < X Ratio Line — Draws the Y = X diagonal Drawing a crosshair at the average Select Both on the Average Line to draw a crosshair at the center of mass of the data distribution. The same style, color, and shade settings apply to both the vertical and horizontal lines. Continuous axes only Reference lines, symmetry shading and the ratio line require a numeric scale. The X Axis and Y Axis cards control the scale, tick labels, and title of each axis.

Each axis accepts either a measure or a category: Drop a measure (numeric value) → the axis is continuous and behaves like a classic XY scatter scale. Drop a column / category (text or discrete value) → the axis becomes categorical: one evenly spaced column (or row) per distinct value, labeled with the category name. You can mix the two — for example a category on Y and a measure on X produces a horizontal "table rows" layout (one row per category, the measure as the score along X). Settings that apply to continuous axes only Range Min/Max, Logarithmic, Origin, Display Units and Decimal Places have no effect on a categorical axis. Likewise, the zoom inset and the analytic overlays that need a numeric scale (constant lines, symmetry shading, ratio line, min/max/median/average lines) are automatically disabled on the affected axis.

Putting a category on both axes turns the scatter into a presence / absence matrix: each cell shows whether a given combination of the two categories exists in the data. It is an effective way to spot which combinations are present and which are missing. Overlap is intentional here When both axes are categorical, several rows that share the same pair of categories land on the same cell and overlap. That is exactly what makes this a presence/absence view: you read whether a combination exists, not how many rows it contains. Use the Size or Color encodings, or a legend, if you need to distinguish the points within a cell.

The zoom inset is one of the most distinctive features of the Smart Scatter Plot. It magnifies a selected rectangular region of the chart and displays it as an enlarged inset — making it easy to explore dense clusters of points without losing the overall context. Interactive Zoom — even in reading mode Unlike features that only work in edit mode, the zoom inset is fully interactive in reading mode. Report consumers can explore dense data areas without any editing permissions. This makes it ideal for published reports and dashboards.

Because values are expressed as percentages, the zoom inset maintains its relative position and size when the chart is resized or printed at a different resolution. Automatic positioning In most cases, you do not need to set these values manually. When the zoom inset is enabled, you can drag and resize both the source region and the inset window directly on the chart. The percentage values update automatically. Manual entry is only useful when you want to replicate the exact same zoom configuration across multiple charts. Continuous axes only The zoom inset relies on a numeric, invertible scale, so it is available only when both axes are continuous (measures).
